newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urged to raise East Timor issue.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urged to raise East Timor issue.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was urged by 15 U.S. senators on Monday to raise the issue of East Timor with Indonesian President Suharto when they meet next week at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Manila.

"We believe that the occasion of your meeting with President Suharto at the APEC summit offers an important opportunity to raise the issue of a United Nations-sponsored self-determination referendum for the people of East Timor," the senators wrote.
Senators signing the letter included Massachusetts Democrat Edward Kennedy, Wisconsin Democrat Russ Feingold and Rhode Island Republican John Chafee.
They expressed concern about reports of substantial human rights violations by the Indonesian government in East Timor.
Indonesian troops occupied the former Portuguese colony in December 1975. East Timor was declared Indonesia's 27th province the following July in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
